help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: When a download is paused: choosing a different source for a file whose download has already started is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The current service and current source are still displayed, and next to the service name a message indicates where the file will go, for example Switching to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. Choosing again replaces this message; choosing the source that is already in use removes it. After resuming, the message reads Switching to … until the switch takes effect, and then disappears. If the paused files of a download would go to different places or the destination is not known, no destination is displayed. A file whose download never started has nothing to hand over, so its new source will simply be used when the download starts. Choosing a service while paused works as described above, except that the download remains paused: a service that can take over the link in use takes it over immediately (visible on the badge), and a service that must first prepare a copy displays Preparing: … and takes over the download only after resuming. These messages appear in the rows of the “Download activity” section and on the “Downloads” page; both kinds can be visible at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. By default it is on for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off for TorBox, which has stricter torrent limits. When it is on, the service also adds torrents delivered by another service so it is ready to take over if needed, and after a download is switched to another service, the torrent already started is kept as a backup instead of being deleted. This uses up the account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot reclaims it first. To keep this service's slots for its own downloads, turn the switch off: its backup torrents will then be deleted. A choice already saved is kept.

Backup torrents use up the account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot reclaims them first.

help.howitworks.adding_same_thing.if_add.backTranslation: If a magnet, a {file_type} file, NZB or Metalink is added that DebridPulse is already working on (including one whose download failed and that has not been removed from the list), the message Already queued appears and the existing download is kept instead of starting a second one. Web links are always added as a new download. Once a download has completed, been cancelled or been removed from the list, adding the same source again starts a new download. When it turns out that two downloads are fetching the same content, DebridPulse can merge them; the merged download then has the status Merged. When DebridPulse cannot prove that they match, the merged download instead has the status Merged · Unverified. Merging does not change who requested the download: each account's request remains separate.

help.settings.access_integrations.integr.backTranslation: Integration accounts are for automation and cannot sign in to these pages. help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: The User accounts section shows each person with their role, sign-in method and whether the account is enabled. The Add local account button creates an account with a username and password. A role changed in the Edit user window takes effect immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role, without signing them out. Each person has a DebridPulse username, separate from the display name: an OIDC account receives it at first sign-in, and local password sign-in is done with exactly this name; the pencil icon next to it in the Edit user window title lets you change it and keeps the saved password. Clicking an account's name opens its details and activity, where a pending request can be withdrawn individually. The Disable and Delete account buttons first show how many pending download requests the account has; those requests are withdrawn, a transfer that someone else also asked for continues, and completed downloads are never touched. Disabling an account also ends its sign-in sessions and stops its tokens; deleting keeps the account's history and erases its own notification settings. If the OIDC identity of a deleted account signs in again, it gets a new account that stays disabled until it is enabled. The Merge button combines two or more accounts into one, chosen to be kept; two accounts with the same verified email address are flagged, but only merging can combine them. DebridPulse always keeps at least one working Admin; you cannot change your own role or disable your own account.
